channel.title: Fonju Law Firm — Insights
channel.description: Practical legal insights on Cameroonian and OHADA business law from Fonju Law Firm, Douala.

item.title: Registering a Company in Cameroon: What the Process Actually Looks Like
item.description: The official timeline says a few days. The realistic timeline depends on decisions you make before you ever reach the registry. Here is the sequence that works.

item.title: OHADA Explained: The Legal Framework Behind Every Cameroonian Business Deal
item.description: Seventeen countries, one commercial code and a supranational court that can overturn your national judgment. A practical orientation for foreign and local businesses.

item.title: Buying Land in Cameroon: Seven Checks Before You Pay a Deposit
item.description: Land is the most disputed asset in Cameroon and the most frequently mis-sold. Almost every failure traces back to a check that was skipped before the deposit.

item.title: Dismissing an Employee in Cameroon: The Procedure That Protects the Employer
item.description: Employers rarely lose dismissal cases because the reason was bad. They lose because the procedure was incomplete. The file has to be finished before anyone is told anything.

item.title: One Filing, Seventeen Countries: A Practical Guide to OAPI Trade Marks
item.description: Cameroonian businesses have access to a regional registration system that is genuinely powerful and consistently underused. Here is how to use it well.

item.title: Arbitration or Court? Choosing a Dispute Resolution Clause That Works
item.description: The dispute resolution clause is negotiated last, in five minutes, by tired people. It then determines the entire economics of any dispute that follows.

item.title: Foreign Investment in Cameroon: Structures, Incentives and Getting Profits Out
item.description: Investors ask about incentives first. They should ask about repatriation first, because that is the constraint that shapes the whole structure.

item.title: Data Protection for Cameroonian Businesses: Where to Start
item.description: Enterprise customers and foreign partners now refuse to contract without adequate data terms. Compliance has quietly become a sales requirement.

item.title: iGaming in Central Africa: What Operators Should Expect from the Regulator
item.description: Online gaming is growing faster than the legislation written to govern it. Operators who engage early consistently secure better terms than those who regularise later.
